title: Construction Marketing Ideas to Scale From £1M to £5M
meta_description: Construction marketing ideas for UK builders turning over £1M+: sort the systems first, get the right clients through the door, and convert without discounting.
h1: Construction Marketing Ideas to Scale From £1M to £5M
hero_subtitle: A practical guide for builders already turning over serious money and stalled.

intro.answer: Word of mouth got you to £1M. It will not get you to £5M. A satisfied client mentioning your name is fine, but it is luck with a time delay, not a growth strategy.

image.alt: A construction business owner planning the marketing that takes the company past £1M

intro.roadmap: This guide is aimed at businesses already running a team and multiple projects, and wondering why growth has stalled despite the work being good. It covers the systems that come first, getting the right clients through the door, converting without discounting, delivering so the next job follows, and the final push to £5M.

briefing.title: The Problem Is the Pipeline, Not the Work
briefing.intro: Almost every builder stuck below £5M is doing good work. That is exactly why it is confusing. The quality is not the constraint. The constraint is that the flow of the right enquiries is accidental, so the business cannot plan around it.

panels.heading: Why has growth stalled if the work is good?
paragraphs: Because a pipeline built on referrals cannot be turned up. It arrives when it arrives, at whatever value the referrer happens to send, and it stops without warning when one relationship changes.
The businesses pushing through to £3M and £4M run the pipeline the way they run a site: with a method, a sequence, and someone accountable for it.

panels.heading: Sort these before adding any marketing
paragraphs: Spending on marketing before the basics are in place just fills a leaking bucket faster.
steps: Get a proper CRM in place, so enquiries stop living in an inbox.
Fix quoting, which is where most builders quietly lose money.
Then open the channels: LinkedIn, your Google presence, content and case studies.
Then convert deliberately, without being the cheapest, and follow up consistently.

review.label: Worth knowing
review.text: None of this needs a large budget. It needs the fundamentals done in order, which is what separates a £1M business from one heading for £5M.
